subject: Request: Temporary latency SLO grace & staged rollout plan for Hosted API
messages:
From: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@finedge.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Lee <tom.lee@finedge.com>
Date: 2026-05-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted API latency SLO — temporary measurement grace during migration

Hi Mina,

Quick context: we have a scheduled migration of our CDN/edge routing (internal cutover) the weekend of June 5–6 that will temporarily change request patterns to Redwood's Hosted API for a subset (~18% peak) of traffic while we ramp. We expect short-lived latency spikes as connections warm and routing stabilizes.

Can Redwood provide a short-term concession on p95 measurement semantics for that window? Specifically, FinEdge is hoping for either a temporary grace period where p95 breaches during the migration window do not trigger credits, or a time-boxed change to the measurement window (e.g., use a 1-hour aggregation window instead of the standard 5-minute rolling window) for the affected region.

What we need from you to proceed with procurement is:
- A written description of the proposed SLO accommodation and timeframe
- Any operational controls you require (traffic tagging, outage windows, contact points)
- Confirmation whether this change would be visible in the Console (so our Ops team can correlate)

Attached is our migration runbook (FinEdge_SLO_Request_v1.pdf) with traffic estimates and cutover timeline.

Thanks — appreciate a short response so we can align procurement and our internal comms.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Jones
Head of Platform Reliability, FinEdge

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@finedge.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-05-20T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API latency SLO — temporary measurement grace during migration

Hi Sarah — thanks for the runbook and the heads-up. We can accommodate a short, time-boxed SLO carveout with a clear operational playbook. Below is a proposed approach that balances your need to avoid spurious credits with our obligation to preserve SLO integrity for other customers.

Proposal (summary)
- Grace window: 48 hours of explicit carveout per region, applied to the migration dates you indicated (June 5 00:00 UTC–June 6 23:59 UTC).
- Measurement adjustment: During the carveout window we will:
  * Temporarily stop counting p95 breaches toward monthly credit calculations for affected routes.
  * Continue recording raw latency metrics (p50/p95) and mark them as "carveout" in the Console so both teams can analyze impact.
- Rollout guardrails: staged traffic ramp with canary monitoring — we require traffic tagging or a distinguishable route header so we can isolate the affected traffic. Suggested ramp: 1% for 2 hours, 10% for 6 hours, then full (~18%) with 72-hour observation.
- Visibility: Console will show a new dataset tag (finedge-migration-2026-06) and we will provide a shared dashboard access for FinEdge for the carveout period.
- Post-window: A 7-day observation period where we leave the standard SLOs active (i.e., breaches count again) but hold off on immediate credits while we jointly review telemetry. If we observe persistent regression outside those 7 days, normal SLO rules apply.

Operational asks from FinEdge
- Provide a short-lived header value (X-FE-Migration: june-2026) or route-level flag to identify traffic.
- Share exact cutoff timestamps and a single point-of-contact for urgent incidents.

Legal/contract note: We can treat this as an addendum to the existing contract that explicitly states the carveout is time-boxed and limited to the scenarios described. Our billing team will need a signed amendment (we can draft).

If that approach sounds acceptable, I'll loop in SRE/Platform (Karthik) to add the tracing and dashboard hooks and have Legal draft the amendment. I attached a concise summary to speed sign-off.

Thanks — Mina
Mina Haddad
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@finedge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-05-20T14:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API latency SLO — temporary measurement grace during migration

Adding SRE notes and technical constraints so we can operationalize Mina's proposal.

SRE checklist (our requirements)
- Traffic identification: Must be either the header Mina suggested (X-FE-Migration) or a separate endpoint. No implicit IP-based identification.
- Region scoping: Carveout will be scoped to the region(s) you indicate; we can only apply measurement flags where we control the ingress (us-west-2, us-east-1).
- Monitoring: We'll enable a dedicated dashboard with:
  * 1-minute and 5-minute heatmaps for p50/p95 by route tag
  * Request-level logging for any request with latency > 2s (sampled) for 72 hours post-cutover
  * Alerting on error-rate > 0.5% or sustained p95 > 1.5x baseline for 30 minutes (separate from credits)
- Fallback: Because you will be in a hybrid routing state during migration, we require automatic fallback policies enabled on your side to reduce traffic to Redwood by 50% if error-rate alerts trigger.

On measurement semantics: we will mark metrics as "carveout" and exclude them from the monthly credit calculation, but we will keep the standard rolling windows active for internal monitoring. This preserves accountability (we still see the degradation) while avoiding immediate financial impact for the migration window.

Engineering timeline: If FinEdge provides the header and contact details by EOD Monday (2026-05-24), we can provision the dashboard and tagging rules and run a test canary earlier in the week of May 31.

--Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, SRE & Platform, Redwood Inference

Mina / Karthik — this all looks good and aligned with our expectations. Two quick confirmations:
- We will add the header (X-FE-Migration: june-2026) and provide exact timestamps by EOD Monday 2026-05-24.
- FinEdge accepts the 48-hour carveout window for June 5–6 and the 7-day post-observation period.

I've attached the signed amendment for your Legal (FinEdge_signed_amendment.pdf) and completed the DocuSign envelope: https://app.docusign.com/FinEdge/amps/12345

Tom and I will be available on-call during the cutover; we'll share cell numbers privately if needed. Please proceed with dashboard provisioning and tagging rules.

Thanks for the quick turnaround — Sarah
Sarah Jones
